title: caa-challenge-2025-solution
subtitle: Saved 2025 models behind the AssurPrime baseline (ENS Challenge Data #161)
description:
# CAA challenge: the 2025 winning solution (saved models)

Saved models from the solution that took first place in the Crédit Agricole Assurances *Data Science Academy* hackathon (spring 2025), ranked on [ENS Challenge Data #161](https://challengedata.ens.fr/challenges/161), "AssurPrime". They were fitted in 2025 with AutoCarver 7.0.5 and XGBoost.

This dataset exists so that the 2025 baseline quoted in the article can be re-scored by anyone. The code and the article's other numbers are in [github.com/mdefrance/caa-challenge](https://github.com/mdefrance/caa-challenge). The challenge data itself is in the companion dataset [caa-challenge-2025](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mariodefrance/caa-challenge-2025).

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `cm_carver_freq_tschuprowt.json` | AutoCarver 7.0.5 `BinaryCarver` on the claim amount `CM`. It defines the stratified train/dev split of the 2025 severity model. |
| `018_carver.json` | AutoCarver 7.0.5 `ContinuousCarver` applied to the severity model's features. |
| `018_best_features.json` | The feature list the 2025 selector kept for the severity model. |
| `019_xgboost.json` | The 2025 severity model (XGBoost regressor), as saved. |
| `frequency_2025_handoff.csv.gz` | The 2025 frequency model's output on train and dev, keyed on `ID`: `pred_sum` (expected claim count) plus the columns the severity model reads. The original file carried every carved column (2.4 GB); only those the replay uses are kept, with their values copied as text. |

## How to re-score the 2025 baseline

1. Clone the repository and download both datasets.
2. Build the 2025 environment: `uv venv --python 3.11 .venv-705` then `uv pip install --python .venv-705 -r requirements-705.txt`. The carvers only load under AutoCarver 7.0.5.
3. Put the challenge CSVs and `Incendies.csv` in the repository's `data/` folder, then run `.venv-705/Scripts/python.exe tools/replay_2025_charge.py --artifacts <this dataset's folder>`.

The script re-fits nothing. Its control is the severity dev RMSE recorded by the 2025 notebook, 6613.817574532793. When the replay matches it, the `CHARGE` dev RMSE computed alongside it (6639.9) comes from the same models.
